mechanism_narrative: The four-week plateau in WORKPLACES at roughly -47 with a small week-on-week improvement in the final week marks a slow, always-on return of commuting routines; each incremental commuter re-engages incidental retail and food-service spend, so RETAIL_REC drifts upward over the next four weeks from a deeply depressed base.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -47.6 to -47.1 in the final week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than its last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES continues to sit within 1 point of -47.1.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week jump in PARKS of more than 8 percentage points (as observed from -47.9 to -38.0) signals that households are re-normalizing discretionary outdoor trips; because outdoor trips are chained with errands, RETAIL_REC rises over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -47.9 at t-1w to -38.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the two weeks after a PARKS week-on-week jump exceeding 8 points, RETAIL_REC declines or stays flat relative to its prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: The retail recovery requires TRANSIT and WORKPLACES to improve jointly: transit restoration without office return leaves footfall corridors empty, and office return without transit access cannot be served. Only their joint improvement lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved in the final week
regime_hint: partial reopening with mixed commuting capacity
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by at least 1 point from t-0w.
